an4.13:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four right strivings.
an4.13:1.3: (1) Here, a bhikkhu generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen bad unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives.
an4.13:1.4: (2) He generates desire for the abandoning of arisen bad unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives.
an4.13:1.5: (3) He generates desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives.
an4.13:1.6: (4) He generates desire for the persistence of arisen wholesome states, for their non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives.
an4.13:1.7: These are the four right strivings.”
an4.13:2.1:
Those who strive rightly
overcome the realm of Māra;
an4.13:2.2:
they are unattached,
gone beyond fear of birth and death.
an4.13:2.3:
They are contented and unstirred,
having conquered Māra and his mount;
an4.13:2.4:
those happy ones have overcome
all Namuci’s armies.
